points.description: States that a very large number of hidden layers causes overfitting (model fits training data too closely), using the term 'overfitting', and that it fails to generalise to new/unseen data (low training error but high testing error).
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if 'overfitting' is named but the poor generalisation / training-vs-testing error contrast is missing or vague.

points.description: States that the model has a high variance problem (the term 'high variance' must be used), together with the slow backpropagation / slow training that results from many layers.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if only one of 'high variance' or 'slow backpropagation' is stated precisely.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the exact terms: overfitting with failure to generalise (low training error, high test error), and high variance with slow backpropagation. Part marks only when one of the two required elements in a point is precise. Vague statements such as 'model gets complex' or 'bad performance', or any wrong claim such as underfitting or high bias, earn nothing for that point.
